```{r setup}
#| include: false

source(here::here("quarto", "_shared", "_setup.R"))

# Compact theme for report plots
report_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", color = AZ_navy),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7, color = AZ_darkgrey),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 6),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.box.margin = margin(-5, 0, 0, 0),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 4, 2, 2, "pt"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 5.5, hjust = 0, color = AZ_darkgrey)
  )

# --- Data loading (multi-DCO, same pattern as presentation) ---

# Part E conditional KM across DCOs
cond_km_part_e <- bind_rows(
  apr25 = tar_read(all_tumor_ssls_cond_km_rvar_ctdna_apr25),
  aug25 = tar_read(all_tumor_ssls_cond_km_rvar_ctdna_aug25),
  jan26 = tar_read(all_tumor_ssls_cond_km_rvar_ctdna_jan26),
  .id = "dco"
) |>
  filter(
    fct_match(variable, "parts"),
    fct_match(cond_group_name, "part_e"),
    fct_match(fit_type, "posterior")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    km_est = cond_sample_km_est,
    dco = fct_recode(factor(dco), "Apr25" = "apr25", "Aug25" = "aug25", "Jan26" = "jan26"),
    trial = "sclc"
  )

# Observed KM for Part E across DCOs
obs_km_part_e <- bind_rows(
  apr25 = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_part_e_ctdna_apr25),
  aug25 = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_part_e_ctdna_aug25),
  jan26 = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_part_e_ctdna_jan26),
  .id = "dco"
) |>
  filter(fct_match(btype, "ub")) |>
  select(!quantiles) |>
  unnest(km_data) |>
  mutate(
    dco = fct_recode(factor(dco), "Apr25" = "apr25", "Aug25" = "aug25", "Jan26" = "jan26")
  )

# Median PFS data (multi-DCO)
quant_pfs_list <- list(
  apr25 = tar_read(all_tumor_ssls_trial_quant_pfs_ctdna_apr25),
  aug25 = tar_read(all_tumor_ssls_trial_quant_pfs_ctdna_aug25),
  jan26 = jan26_quant_pfs_data
)
cond_quant_pfs_list <- list(
  apr25 = tar_read(all_tumor_ssls_cond_quant_pfs_ctdna_apr25),
  aug25 = tar_read(all_tumor_ssls_cond_quant_pfs_ctdna_aug25),
  jan26 = jan26_cond_quant_pfs_data
)
obs_km_list <- list(
  apr25 = list(
    all = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_ctdna_apr25),
    pdl1_naive = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_pdl1_naive_ctdna_apr25),
    pdl1 = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_pdl1_ctdna_apr25),
    naive = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_naive_ctdna_apr25)
  ),
  aug25 = list(
    all = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_ctdna_aug25),
    pdl1_naive = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_pdl1_naive_ctdna_aug25),
    pdl1 = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_pdl1_ctdna_aug25),
    naive = tar_read(km_trial_pfs_naive_ctdna_aug25)
  ),
  jan26 = list(
    all = jan26_obs_km_all,
    pdl1_naive = jan26_obs_km_pdl1_naive,
    pdl1 = jan26_obs_km_pdl1,
    naive = jan26_obs_km_first_line
  )
)

# LFO confusion matrix data
oos_confusion_matrix <- tar_read(oos_confusion_matrix_ctdna_jan26, store = lfo_store)
full_oos_confusion_matrix <- tar_read(full_oos_confusion_matrix_ctdna_jan26, store = lfo_store)

# --- Save plots to files for LaTeX minipage inclusion ---
plot_dir <- here::here("quarto", "reports", "_plots")
dir.create(plot_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Plot A: Part E PFS Forecast by DCO
p_a <- cond_km_part_e |>
  base_plot_km(
    obs_km_data = NULL,
    km_est = km_est,
    group = fit_type,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_step(
    aes(x = t, y = s, linetype = "Observed KM"),
    linewidth = 0.8,
    alpha = 0.5,
    color = AZ_plum,
    data = obs_km_part_e
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual("", values = c("Observed KM" = "solid")) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    "Months",
    breaks = months_to_weeks(seq(0, 60, 12)),
    label = label_weeks_to_months
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous("PFS", labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = AZ_platinum) +
  guides(color = "none", fill = "none", alpha = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~dco, ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "A: Part E PFS Forecast by Data Cutoff") +
  report_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(-2, 0, 0, 0),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 7, face = "bold")
  )
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "plot_a.pdf"), p_a, width = 5.2, height = 3.0, device = cairo_pdf)

# Plot B: RECIST Confusion Matrix
p_b <- plot_oos_confusion_matrix(oos_confusion_matrix, add_caption = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "B: RECIST Prediction Sensitivity"
  ) +
  report_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm")
  )
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "plot_b.pdf"), p_b, width = 5.2, height = 3.0, device = cairo_pdf)

# Plot C: Median PFS by DCO
p_c <- plot_median_pfs_by_dco(
  "sample",
  quant_pfs_list,
  cond_quant_pfs_list,
  obs_km_list,
  show_observed = TRUE
) +
  labs(title = "C: Median PFS Stability Across Data Cutoffs") +
  report_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, -4, 0),
    legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, -4, 0)
  )
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "plot_c.pdf"), p_c, width = 5.2, height = 3.0, device = cairo_pdf)

# Plot D: RECIST Sensitivity Over Time
p_d <- full_oos_confusion_matrix |>
  plot_recist_sensitivity_over_time(
    base_size = 8,
    caption = "Ribbon = \u00B11 SE of cumulative mean across LFO folds."
  ) +
  labs(title = "D: RECIST Sensitivity Over Time") +
  report_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(-2, 0, 0, 0)
  )
ggsave(file.path(plot_dir, "plot_d.pdf"), p_d, width = 5.2, height = 3.0, device = cairo_pdf)
```

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
{\fontsize{18}{22}\selectfont\bfseries\textcolor{aznavy}{PIONEER: SCLC-01 Bayesian Forecasting}}\\[4pt]
{\fontsize{10}{13}\selectfont\textcolor{aznavy}{Early Trial Outcome Predictions via Hierarchical Tumor Dynamics Modeling}}\\[3pt]
{\footnotesize Karim Naguib, Roger Berché, Antonia Bevan, Haroon Hasan, Jessica Davies, Paul Metcalfe \hfill February 2026}
\end{center}
\vspace{-2pt}
{\color{azgold}\rule{\textwidth}{2pt}}
\vspace{2pt}
\noindent
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.28\textwidth}
\raggedright
\textcolor{aznavy}{\textsf{\textbf{Overview}}}
\vspace{3pt}
{\small
PIONEER is a Bayesian forecasting system for predicting progression-free survival (PFS) and RECIST response in oncology trials. The model integrates patient-level tumor size dynamics with a competing-risks survival framework, producing probabilistic forecasts that extend beyond the observed censoring horizon.
\vspace{3pt}
A semi-mechanistic state-space model decomposes each patient's tumor trajectory into treatment-sensitive and resistant components. These trajectories drive RECIST classifications and, jointly with a proportional hazards submodel for non-target events, generate PFS predictions.
}
\vspace{6pt}
\textcolor{aznavy}{\textsf{\textbf{Key Findings}}}
\vspace{2pt}
{\small
\begin{itemize}
\setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
\item \textbf{Reliable early forecasts}: PFS predictions remain stable across three data cutoffs (Apr 2025 -- Jan 2026), with decreasing uncertainty as data matures.
\item \textbf{High RECIST accuracy}: Out-of-sample sensitivity of 70--80\% across CR, PR, SD, and PD categories, validated by leave-future-out cross-validation.
\item \textbf{Forecast stability}: Median PFS estimates are consistent across DCOs, confirming that early predictions are not revised as more data accrues.
\item \textbf{3--6 month lead time}: The model provides actionable endpoint forecasts months before traditional observational analyses.
\end{itemize}
}
\vspace{6pt}
\textcolor{aznavy}{\textsf{\textbf{Role of Historical Data}}}
\vspace{3pt}
{\small
The model employs a three-level hierarchy (population $\to$ trial $\to$ patient) that enables principled borrowing from four historical trials: HISTORICAL, ARCTIC, PEARL, and ATLANTIC. This hierarchical structure is critical early in SCLC-01 when patient-level data is sparse---historical trials anchor population-level parameters while SCLC-01 data progressively informs trial- and patient-specific effects.
}
\vspace{6pt}
\textcolor{aznavy}{\textsf{\textbf{Conclusions}}}
\vspace{3pt}
{\small
PIONEER demonstrates that mechanistic Bayesian modeling can deliver reliable trial outcome forecasts substantially earlier than conventional analysis. This approach has the potential to accelerate go/no-go decisions in oncology drug development while maintaining rigorous uncertainty quantification.
}
\end{minipage}%
```
